Subject: GPU headroom validation for closing deal: Atlas Labs

Team —

Atlas Labs is pushing to close next week and legal/finance are on fast-track. They want a technical confirmation that we can meet a 99th percentile latency SLO for their planned traffic and a short runway reserved while they finalize procurement. Quick summary below (attachments: atlas_deal_summary.pdf, expected_traffic.xlsx):

- Deal: Atlas Labs (production model host)
- Go-live target: 2027-01-15 (pilot + staged ramp)
- Peak forecast: ~60 sustained inference req/s during peak hour, bursts up to 140 req/s for short windows
- Model and profile: redwood-13b-quant (kv-cache heavy, 4k prompt windows)
- Latency SLO: 99th <= 350ms for single-turn generation (no tool calls)
- Requested: provisional headroom / capacity window: 2026-12-15 -> 2027-03-15

Ask: can infra confirm whether we have the headroom to guarantee the SLO with the above profile, and if not, what minimal fleet carve (GPUs / nodes) we should earmark as a provisional soft-reserve while legal finishes paperwork? If useful, open an internal CAP ticket and tag me — I can escalate to Marissa for sign-off.

Notes: Atlas is sensitive to any additional latency from multi-tenant co-location; they prefer a dedicated slice but will accept a pinned dedicated pool if we can meet latency and isolation requirements.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference

Rishi —

Thanks for the details and attachments. Quick preliminary read: the redwood-13b-quant with a warm KV cache and 4k windows is quite cache/memory heavy but should be achievable with pinned capacity. A few clarifying Qs (please confirm):

1) Is the 60 req/s sustained for single-token streaming or average-turn generation (~200 tokens)?
2) Will Atlas enable prefix caching from day 1 (i.e., many repeated prompts) or is traffic expected to be highly varied?

Prelim calc (ballpark):
- If average turn ~200 tokens and effective batching of 6-8 across requests, we can target 350ms 99th with either:
  * ~4 H100s (pinned) with dedicated pool and aggressive batching OR
  * ~8 A100-style nodes if H100s not available.

I'll spin up a quick headroom model and attach a calc (gpu_headroom_calc.csv). My recommendation: open CAP-4521 (I've created the Jira placeholder) and request a provisional soft-reserve for 4 H100s in us-west for the 12/15–03/15 window. That gives us a buffer for validation and early ramp. If batch-friendly traffic turns out lower variance, we can downscale during steady-state.

I can also run a short perf test against a staging copy if Atlas can provide a small sample request set.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Infrastructure Sales Engineer
karthik_iyer@redwood.inference

Thanks Karthik — good questions. Answers below and a couple of updates from Atlas (forwarded summary from Evan):

- Average turn: ~220 tokens (their initial benchmark)
- Traffic shape: a mix — roughly 70% repeatable patterns (prefix reuse) and 30% unique queries; they expect prefix caching to matter but not eliminate variance
- Bursts: customers call bursts are tied to business events; they expect several 2–4 minute spikes per day
- Atlas confirmed they can provide a 1k-sample request corpus for perf testing; Evan copied below.

Given that, locking a soft-reserve of 4 H100s in us-west as you suggested sounds right to me. Please proceed to open CAP-4521 and mark it "soft-hold - sales priority". I'll prepare a short note for Marissa to authorize provisional carve if infra signs off on the perf results.
